topic_title: Direct & Indirect Speech (Narration) with SBI PO Level Error Detection

intro_payload.title: Narration: Direct & Indirect Speech
intro_payload.subtitle: Master Sentence Transformation for BPSC, SSC, Railway, Bank PO & BPSC TRE Exams
learning_outcomes: Convert Assertive, Interrogative, Imperative, Exclamatory & Optative sentences from Direct to Indirect Speech
Master Tense Backshift Rules & the Universal Truth exception
Learn complete Pronoun, Time-word & Place-word conversion tables
Handle Modal Verb changes (can-could, will-would, must-had to)
Master tricky reporting verbs: suggest, propose, insist, let's, exclaim, wish
Crack SBI PO / Bank PO level Error Detection questions on Narration

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, socho tumne dost se kaha - 'Main kal school nahi aaunga.' Ab tum teacher ko wahi baat bata rahe ho. Tum kya bologe?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir main bolunga... 'Usne kaha ki wo kal school nahi aayega.' Par sir, 'kal' to 'aayega' mein badal gaya!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi pakड़a! Jab hum kisi ke EXACT shabd, quotation marks ke andar bolte hain, use kehte hain 'Direct Speech'. Aur jab hum apne shabdon mein, bina quotation ke, wahi baat report karte hain - use kehte hain 'Indirect Speech' ya 'Reported Speech'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Toh sir jaise main mummy ka message papa ko apne words mein sunata hoon, wo Indirect Speech hua?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exactly! Ab dhyan se suno - Indirect speech ke do parts hote hain. Pehla part 'Reporting Verb' - jaise 'said', 'told' - jo batata hai ki kisne bola. Doosra part 'Reported Speech' - jisme actual baat hoti hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'said' aur 'told' dono same nahi hain kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut achha doubt! Agar 'said' ke baad koi person mention nahi hai to wahi rehta hai, lekin agar person mention hai jaise 'said to Raju', to wo 'told Raju' ban jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh 'said to' hamesha 'told' mein badalta hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan, aur ek golden rule yaad rakho - Direct Speech mein hum quotation marks (' ') use karte hain, lekin Indirect Speech mein NO quotation marks. Comma hat jaata hai aur 'that' add hota hai (statements mein).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'that' hamesha lagana zaroori hai kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Zaroori nahi, optional hota hai - 'He said that he was tired' ya 'He said he was tired' dono correct hain. Par exam paper mein 'that' wala option hi safe answer hota hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Okay sir, samajh gaya - quotation hatao, comma hatao, 'that' lagao!

quiz_payload.question: Which is the correct definition of Reported (Indirect) Speech?

options.text: The exact words spoken, enclosed in quotation marks
Speech reported in someone else's own words, without quotation marks

quiz_payload.explanation: Reported/Indirect speech conveys the meaning of what was said, in our own words, without repeating the exact words or using quotation marks.

quiz_payload.question: Identify the Reporting Verb in: 'Raju told his teacher that he had finished the homework.'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'told' is the Reporting Verb, telling us WHO spoke. 'that he had finished the homework' is the Reported Speech, the actual content.

quiz_payload.question: Convert: Raju said, 'I am happy.' → Raju said that he ____ happy.
quiz_payload.explanation: Since the reporting verb 'said' is in past tense, the present tense 'am' shifts one step back to 'was'. Don't worry, we'll master this Tense Backshift rule in the next module!

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Foundation strong ho gayi Raju! Ab asli grammar engine start karte hain!

guess_payload.question: Raju said, 'I am tired.' Sita is now reporting this sentence to someone else. Will the word 'I' remain 'I' in Indirect Speech?

options.text: No, it changes to 'he' (subject of reporting verb)
It depends on the listener's mood

guess_payload.explanation: 1st person pronouns change according to the SUBJECT of the reporting verb. Since 'Raju' (he) is the one speaking, 'I' becomes 'he'. This is the Person Rule of Pronoun Change - let's learn it fully!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi guess tha! Yaad rakho ye pura rule: 1st person pronoun (I, we, my, our) badal ke REPORTING VERB ke SUBJECT jaisa ho jaata hai. 2nd person pronoun (you, your) badal ke REPORTING VERB ke OBJECT jaisa ho jaata hai. 3rd person pronoun (he, she, they) mein koi change NAHI hota.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye thoda confuse kar raha hai... ek clear example dijiye na!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Dekho: Raju said, 'I am tired.' Yahan subject hai Raju, so 'I' badal ke 'he' ban jaayega → Raju said that he was tired.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh 1st person hamesha subject Raju jaisa hi ban jaayega, chahe wo 'main' ho ya 'hum'?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab 2nd person dekho: Raju said to Sita, 'You are clever.' Yahan reporting verb ka object hai Sita, so 'you' badlega Sita ke roop mein → Raju told Sita that she was clever.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh! Toh 'you' hamesha wahi person banega jisko baat boli gayi thi, matlab object wala?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exactly! Ye favorite trap hai exams ka - log 'you' ko galti se 'I' bana dete hain. ⭐ BPSC TRE Favorite: is rule pe direct fill-in-blank aata hai!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir samajh gaya - 1st person = subject, 2nd person = object, 3rd person = no change!

quiz_payload.question: Raju said to me, 'I will help you.' → Indirect: Raju told me that ____ would help ____.
quiz_payload.explanation: 'I' (1st person, subject = Raju) → 'he'. 'you' (2nd person, object = speaker/me) → 'me'. Final: Raju told me that he would help me.

quiz_payload.question: He said, 'I have lost my pen.' → He said that ____ had lost ____ pen.
quiz_payload.explanation: Both 'I' and 'my' are 1st person pronouns, so both change to match the subject 'he' - giving 'he' and 'his'.

quiz_payload.question: Statement 1: 2nd person pronoun changes according to the OBJECT of the reporting verb. Statement 2: 3rd person pronoun never changes in indirect speech. Which is/are correct?
quiz_payload.explanation: Both rules are correct as per the standard Pronoun Change Rule of Narration.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Pronoun master ban gaye Raju! Ab Tense ka sabse bada rule seekhte hain!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, jab tum kal ki baat aaj bata rahe ho, kya wahi tense use hoga jo bolne wale ne kal use kiya tha?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir wo to time hi badal gaya na, toh tense bhi badal jaayega shayad?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi socha! Jab reporting verb PAST TENSE mein hoti hai (said, told), to reported speech ka tense bhi ek stair peeche chala jaata hai. Isko kehte hain 'Backshift of Tense'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'ek stair peeche' matlab kya? Table dikhaiye na!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Table yaad karo: Present Simple → Past Simple (is/am/are → was/were). Present Continuous → Past Continuous (is doing → was doing). Present Perfect → Past Perfect (has done → had done).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir itne saare changes! Confuse ho jaunga exam mein!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ek trick yaad rakho - bas ek stair peeche jao: Present family → Past family, Past family → Past Perfect family. Future 'will/shall' → 'would/should'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, matlab har tense apni immediate peechhe wali tense mein chala jaata hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Continue karte hain: Past Simple → Past Perfect (went → had gone). Past Continuous → Past Perfect Continuous (was going → had been going). Aur Past Perfect → NO CHANGE, kyunki wo already sabse peeche wali tense hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir Past Perfect mein to already 'had' laga hai, wo aage kaise jaayega?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exactly sahi pakड़a - Past Perfect ek dead-end hai, usme koi further backshift nahi hota. Ye exam ka bahut common trap hai!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Yaad rakh lunga sir - Past Perfect ka 'full stop' hi hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab sabse important EXCEPTION suno - agar reported speech mein ek UNIVERSAL TRUTH ya HABITUAL FACT ho, jaise 'Sun rises in the East', to tense CHANGE NAHI hota, chahe reporting verb past mein ho!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab sir agar teacher ne kaha 'Sun rises in the east' to indirect mein bhi 'rises' hi rahega, 'rose' nahi banega?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Example: The teacher said that the sun rises in the east. Yahi rule historical facts pe bhi lagta hai - jaise 'Mahatma Gandhi was born in 1869' - already fixed past fact hai, waise hi rahega.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye to exam mein sabse zyada confuse karega, sab log 'that' ke saath tense badal dete honge!

quiz_payload.question: He said, 'I am writing a letter.' → Indirect:

options.text: He said that he is writing a letter
He said that he was writing a letter
He said that he had written a letter
He said that he had been writing a letter

quiz_payload.explanation: Present Continuous ('am writing') shifts one step back to Past Continuous ('was writing').

quiz_payload.question: The teacher said, 'The Earth revolves around the Sun.' → Indirect:

options.text: The teacher said that the Earth revolved around the Sun
The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the Sun
The teacher said that the Earth had revolved around the Sun
The teacher said that the Earth will revolve around the Sun

quiz_payload.explanation: Universal truths never undergo tense backshift, regardless of the reporting verb's tense.

quiz_payload.question: Statement 1: Past Perfect tense does not change further in indirect speech. Statement 2: Universal truths always take tense change according to the reporting verb. Which is correct?
quiz_payload.explanation: Statement 2 is FALSE - universal truths never change tense. This exact trap is a BPSC favorite multi-statement question.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Tense ka boss ban gaye Raju! Ab Time aur Place words ki baari!

guess_payload.question: Rani said, 'I will call you tomorrow.' If this is reported the NEXT day, will the word 'tomorrow' remain 'tomorrow' in indirect speech?
guess_payload.explanation: When the reporting verb is in the past tense, time/place words referring to the speaker's 'present' shift to distance-words. 'tomorrow' → 'the next day'.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi guess tha! Ab poora table yaad karo: now→then, today→that day, tomorrow→the next day/the following day, yesterday→the previous day/the day before, ago→before, last night→the previous night, next week→the following week.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir itna sab yaad rakhna padega? Koi shortcut?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Shortcut hai - jitna bhi 'is/present' se related word hai, use 'that/distance' wale word se badal do. Practice se automatic ho jaata hai!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Okay sir, ab place words bhi bata dijiye!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Place words bhi badalte hain: here→there, this→that, these→those, come→go. Example: He said, 'I will come here tomorrow.' → He said that he would go there the next day.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'come' 'go' mein kyun badalta hai? Wo to person hi hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Kyunki jab hum kisi third person ko event report karte hain, hum us jagah se door hote hain (perspective badal jaata hai), isliye direction bhi badal jaata hai. Ye pure grammar logic hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Toh 'this→that', 'here→there' - sab distance ke rule pe chal raha hai!

quiz_payload.question: He said, 'I saw her yesterday.' → Indirect:

options.text: He said that he had seen her yesterday
He said that he had seen her the previous day
He said that he saw her the day before
He said that he has seen her the previous day

quiz_payload.explanation: Past Simple 'saw' → Past Perfect 'had seen', and 'yesterday' → 'the previous day'.

quiz_payload.question: She said, 'I will meet you here tomorrow.' → Indirect:

options.text: She said that she would meet me there the next day
She said that she would meet me here tomorrow
She said that she will meet me there the following day
She said that she would meet me here the following day

quiz_payload.explanation: will→would, you→me, here→there, tomorrow→the next day - all four rules applied together.

quiz_payload.question: Which time-word change is INCORRECT?
quiz_payload.explanation: 'ago' changes to 'before', NOT 'later'. This is a common SSC/Railway trap in fill-in-the-blank questions.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Time-Place table pakka ho gaya! Ab Modals ka mahayudh shuru karte hain!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, modals jaise 'can', 'may', 'will', 'must' - ye bhi kaafi change hote hain indirect speech mein. Chalo dekhte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir modal matlab? Wo 'can', 'will' jaise words na?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ye helping verbs hain jo possibility, permission, ability dikhate hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha sir, inka bhi tense jaisa hi table hoga kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Yaad karo: can→could, may→might, will→would, shall→should, must→had to (obligation ke case mein). Ye sabse zyada poochha jaane wala table hai!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'could', 'would', 'should', 'might' already past wale hain, unka kya hoga?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut achha sawal! Agar sentence mein pehle se hi 'could/would/should/might/ought to' use ho, to NO FURTHER CHANGE hota - wo already sabse peeche wale form hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir yaani ye modals bhi Past Perfect jaisa 'dead-end' hain?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi comparison! Ab 'must' ka special rule suno: agar 'must' abhi bhi valid obligation dikhata hai, to 'must' hi rehta hai. Agar past necessity hai jo khatam ho gayi, to 'had to' banta hai. Ye BPSC ka favorite confusion point hai!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir matlab hamesha 'had to' nahi banega?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi pakड़a! Example: He said, 'I must go now' → He said that he had to go then (simple past action report) - exam mein zyadatar 'had to' hi expected answer hota hai, jab tak sentence 'still true' na bataye.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, toh default answer 'had to' rakhna safe hai!

quiz_payload.question: He said, 'I can swim.' → Indirect:

options.text: He said that he can swim
He said that he could swim
He said that he is able to swim
He said that he can be able to swim

quiz_payload.explanation: 'can' shifts to 'could' when the reporting verb is in the past tense.

quiz_payload.question: She said, 'I would help you if I could.' → Indirect:

options.text: She said that she would help me if she could
She said that she would have helped me if she had could
She said that she will help me if she can
She said that she would help him if he can

quiz_payload.explanation: 'would' and 'could' are already past-form modals, so they remain UNCHANGED. Only pronoun changes (I→she, you→me).

quiz_payload.question: Which sentence correctly shows 'must' changing for a past compulsion that's now over?

options.text: He said that he must complete the work
He said that he had to complete the work
He said that he must have completed the work
He said that he should complete the work

quiz_payload.explanation: For simple past reporting of an obligation, 'must' → 'had to' is the standard exam answer.

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Modals bhi fatafat solve kar rahe ho! Ab sab kuch mila ke Assertive sentence banate hain!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab tak jo bhi rules seekhe - tense, pronoun, time/place, modal - sab ek saath istemal hote hain ASSERTIVE sentences (simple statements) mein. Conjunction 'that' use hota hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir Assertive matlab simple statement wale sentences?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan bilkul - jaise 'I am happy', 'He plays cricket' - ye assertive/statement sentences hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ab poora example dikhaiye jisme sab rules mix hon!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Poora example dekho: Rina said, 'I am going to Patna tomorrow.' Step by step: I→she (subject Rina), am going→was going (tense), tomorrow→the next day (time). Final: Rina said that she was going to Patna the next day.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Ohh sir ab sab pieces jud rahe hain! Puzzle jaisa hai ye to!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi bola - Narration hai hi ek puzzle jisme har piece (pronoun+tense+time/place+modal) apni jagah fit hota hai!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir agar sentence negative ho jaise 'I do not like tea' to kya extra rule hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Nahi, negative assertive mein bhi wahi rule chalta hai - bas 'do not/does not' → 'did not' ban jaata hai tense ke hisaab se. She said, 'I do not like tea.' → She said that she did not like tea.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha sir, matlab negative sentence special nahi hai, wahi tense rule follow karega?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Aur ek chhoti baat - 'that' likhna optional hai, lekin exam options mein 'that' wala option hamesha safe rehta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Okay sir, ab main assertive sentence bina galti confidently bana sakta hoon!

quiz_payload.question: Convert: He said, 'I have finished my homework.'

options.text: He said that he has finished his homework
He said that he had finished his homework
He said that he finished his homework
He said that he had finished my homework

quiz_payload.explanation: Present Perfect ('have finished') → Past Perfect ('had finished'); 'my'→'his' as it's a 1st person possessive pronoun.

quiz_payload.question: Convert: She said, 'I do not trust him.'

options.text: She said that she does not trust him
She said that she did not trust him
She said that she had not trusted him
She said that she is not trusting him

quiz_payload.explanation: 'do not' (present simple negative) → 'did not' (past simple negative).

quiz_payload.question: Statement 1: In assertive sentences, using 'that' is compulsory. Statement 2: Negative assertive sentences follow the same tense backshift rule as positive ones. Choose the correct option:
quiz_payload.explanation: 'that' is optional (Statement 1 is false), but negative sentences DO follow the same backshift rule (Statement 2 is true).

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Statements ka expert ban gaye! Ab Questions ka sabse bada trap dekhte hain!

guess_payload.question: Sonu asked Rani, 'Are you coming?' How will this question be correctly reported in indirect speech?

options.text: Sonu asked Rani that she was coming
Sonu asked Rani if she was coming
Sonu asked Rani are you coming
Sonu told Rani if she was coming

guess_payload.explanation: Yes/No questions use 'if' or 'whether' instead of 'that', and the reporting verb 'said' becomes 'asked'. Let's master the full question rules!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi guess tha! Yes/No questions (jinka answer sirf Yes ya No hota hai) mein 'if' ya 'whether' use hota hai, 'that' KABHI NAHI. Reporting verb bhi 'said'→'asked' ban jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'if' aur 'whether' dono chalega? Koi fark nahi?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Exam level pe dono correct maane jaate hain, 'whether' thoda zyada formal hai. Bas yaad rakho - question mark HAT jaata hai aur word order STATEMENT jaisa ho jaata hai!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'word order statement jaisa' matlab kya? Thoda samjhaiye!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Wh-questions (What, Where, When, Who, Why, How) mein 'that/if/whether' kuch nahi lagta - seedha Wh-word se sentence shuru hota hai. Example: He said, 'Where do you live?' → He asked where I lived.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'do you live' se 'I lived' kaise hua? Auxiliary 'do' kahan gaya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut zaroori catch! Indirect question mein hum QUESTION word order nahi, STATEMENT word order use karte hain - matlab 'do/does/did' helping verb hat jaata hai aur normal subject-verb order aata hai. Ye SBI PO ka sabse common trap hai!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Matlab 'where I lived' likhna hai, 'where did I live' nahi? Ye to bilkul ulta lag raha hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi laga, par yehi grammar rule hai - Raju, do golden rules yaad rakho: 1) Question mark (?) hat jaata hai, full stop lagta hai. 2) 'said/said to' → 'asked' ban jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir agar already 'asked' ho reporting verb mein to?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Tab kuch change nahi karna, wahi rehta hai. Bas remember - questions mein KABHI 'that' use mat karna!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye to exam mein sabse zyada marks katega agar bhool gaya!

quiz_payload.question: Convert: She said to him, 'Do you like coffee?'

options.text: She asked him that he liked coffee
She asked him if he liked coffee
She told him if he liked coffee
She asked him do he like coffee

quiz_payload.explanation: Yes/No question: reporting verb becomes 'asked' and connector is 'if'; 'do you like' → 'he liked' (statement order + tense backshift).

quiz_payload.question: Convert: He said, 'Where are you going?'

options.text: He asked where I was going
He asked where was I going
He asked that where I was going
He asked where did I go

quiz_payload.explanation: Wh-question: no 'that', statement word order 'I was going', not inverted question order.

quiz_payload.question: SBI PO style - Spot the error: 'He asked me that where I was going.' (A) He asked me / (B) that where I / (C) was going / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: 'that' is wrongly used with a Wh-word. Correct sentence: 'He asked me where I was going.'

milestone_payload.title: MODULE COMPLETED!
milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Sabse bada trap crack kar liya Raju! Ab Orders aur Requests seekhte hain!

guess_payload.question: The Apartment guard said to the visitors, 'Show your ID card.' What kind of reporting verb should replace 'said' here?
guess_payload.explanation: Commands/Orders use 'ordered' or 'told...to' as reporting verb, and the main verb becomes 'to + base form'. Let's learn all Imperative rules now!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi guess tha! Rule yaad karo: Command/Order ke liye reporting verb 'ordered/commanded' banta hai, aur main verb 'to + base form' (infinitive) mein badal jaata hai. Example: The officer said, 'Stand up!' → The officer ordered them to stand up.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'said' se 'ordered' kaise pata chale? Context se?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan, tone se pata chalta hai - agar sakht order hai to 'ordered/commanded', agar mote se bola hai to 'told'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir agar 'please' bhi ho sentence mein to kya alag rule hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Agar REQUEST hai (please wala), reporting verb 'requested' banta hai aur 'please' word HAT jaata hai. Agar ADVICE hai, 'advised' banta hai. Example: He said, 'Please help me.' → He requested me to help him.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'please' hamesha hataana padega?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan, 'please' word directly hat jaata hai, uski jagah 'requested' verb khud politeness dikha deta hai. Advice ka example: Teacher said, 'You should study daily.' → The teacher advised him to study daily.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha sir, samajh gaya - order='ordered/to', request='requested/to(no please)', advice='advised/to'.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab last part - agar imperative NEGATIVE ho (Don't...), to 'to' se pehle 'not' laga do: 'not to'. Example: He said, 'Don't shout.' → He told them not to shout.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'forbade' bhi kahin sunta hoon, wo bhi use hota hai kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan, strong prohibition ke liye 'forbade' bhi chalta hai (He forbade them to shout), but exam mein zyadatar 'told...not to' hi safe answer hota hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Okay sir, ab imperative sentence ka poora chart yaad ho gaya!

quiz_payload.question: Convert: The teacher said to the students, 'Keep quiet.'

options.text: The teacher told the students to keep quiet
The teacher ordered the students that keep quiet
The teacher said the students to keep quiet
The teacher asked the students keep quiet

quiz_payload.explanation: Command → reporting verb 'told/ordered' + object + 'to + base verb'.

quiz_payload.question: Convert: She said to me, 'Please lend me your pen.'

options.text: She requested me to lend her my pen
She requested me to lend him her pen
She told me please lend her pen
She asked me if I lend her pen

quiz_payload.explanation: 'please' is dropped, reporting verb becomes 'requested', and pronouns change correctly: me(2nd person, object)→me, your(1st person of speaker? actually 'your' belongs to listener=2nd person referring to me)→my.

quiz_payload.question: Convert: The mother said to her son, 'Don't go out in the rain.'

options.text: The mother told her son don't go out in the rain
The mother told her son not to go out in the rain
The mother ordered her son to not going out in the rain
The mother requested her son no to go out in the rain

quiz_payload.explanation: Negative imperative: 'not' is placed before 'to' - 'told...not to go'.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, jab tum khushi se chillate ho 'Wah! Kitna sundar hai!' aur baad mein kisi ko batate ho, kya wahi 'Wah!' bolte ho?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Nahi sir, main bolunga 'maine kaha ki bahut sundar hai' - 'Wah' to nahi bolunga!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Exclamatory sentences (Hurrah!, Alas!, What a.../How...) mein reporting verb 'exclaimed with joy/sorrow/wonder' banta hai aur interjection (Hurrah, Alas, Oh) hat jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ek example dijiye poora convert karke!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Example: He said, 'Hurrah! We have won the match.' → He exclaimed with joy that they had won the match. Aur 'What a beautiful flower it is!' → He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful flower ('What/How' ki jagah 'very' aata hai).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'What a' aur 'How' wale sentence mein 'very' kyun aata hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Kyunki exclamation ki intensity 'very' se express hoti hai jab hum use normal statement mein badalte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha sir, ab 'wishes' wale sentence bhi bata dijiye - jaise 'May you live long!'

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Optative sentences (wishes, prayers) jaise 'May you live long!' ka reporting verb 'wished/prayed' banta hai. Example: He said, 'May God bless you!' → He prayed that God might bless her.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir 'may' yahan 'might' ban gaya, ye bhi ek modal change hai na?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi observation! Optative mein 'may' hamesha 'might' banta hai wish/prayer ke context mein.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ab Exclamatory aur Optative dono clear hain - reporting verb + tone hi sab kuch decide karta hai!

quiz_payload.question: Convert: She said, 'Alas! I have lost my purse.'

options.text: She exclaimed with sorrow that she had lost her purse
She exclaimed that alas she lost her purse
She said with sorrow that she has lost her purse
She exclaimed sadly I have lost my purse

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Alas' shows sorrow, so reporting verb becomes 'exclaimed with sorrow'; interjection removed, tense backshifted.

quiz_payload.question: Convert: The old man said, 'May you be happy forever!'

options.text: The old man wished that I be happy forever
The old man prayed that she might be happy forever
The old man said that she may be happy forever
The old man wished her happy forever

quiz_payload.explanation: Optative sentence: reporting verb 'prayed/wished that', and 'may' → 'might'.

quiz_payload.question: Convert: He said, 'What a lovely morning it is!'

options.text: He exclaimed that it was a lovely morning
He exclaimed that it was a very lovely morning
He said what a lovely morning it was
He exclaimed how lovely the morning is

quiz_payload.explanation: 'What a/How' is replaced by 'very' to preserve the intensity of the exclamation in indirect form.

guess_payload.question: Raju's friends said, 'Let's watch a movie.' Which reporting verb fits best for indirect speech here?
guess_payload.explanation: 'Let's' sentences (suggestions) use 'suggested/proposed' as the reporting verb, followed by 'that + subject + should'.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! 'Let's' sentences ka pattern hai: reporting verb 'suggested/proposed' + 'that + subject + should'. Example: He said, 'Let's go to the market.' → He suggested that they should go to the market.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir aur 'insist' wala kya hota hai? Wo bhi suna hai kahin.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'Insisted' use hota hai jab koi zid karke bole. Example: She said, 'You must apologize.' → She insisted that he must apologize / should apologize.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir insist ke baad bhi 'should' ya 'must' dono chal sakte hain?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan, dono chalte hain context ke hisaab se. Aur ek fixed formula yaad rakho - 'Suggest/Propose' verbs ke baad hamesha 'that + subject + should + base verb' pattern aata hai, chahe original sentence mein 'should' na bhi ho.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir jaise 'Why don't we start early?' - isme to 'should' nahi hai, phir bhi?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi example diya! He said, 'Why don't we start early?' → He suggested that they should start early. Ye ek fixed formula hai jo bahut baar directly poochha jaata hai. ⭐ BPSC TRE Favorite!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ye to yaad rakhna easy hoga, fixed pattern hai!

quiz_payload.question: Convert: He said, 'Let's play football.'

options.text: He suggested that they should play football
He told them to let's play football

quiz_payload.explanation: 'Let's' → 'suggested that + subject + should + base verb'.

quiz_payload.question: Convert: The doctor said, 'You must take rest.'

options.text: The doctor insisted that he must take rest
The doctor suggested him to must take rest
The doctor said he should took rest
The doctor told he must took rest

quiz_payload.explanation: Strong obligation with 'must' from a doctor is best reported as 'insisted that...must take rest'.

quiz_payload.question: Statement 1: 'Suggest/Propose' always take the 'should' pattern in indirect speech. Statement 2: 'Let's' sentences take the reporting verb 'ordered'. Which is correct?
quiz_payload.explanation: Statement 2 is wrong - 'Let's' sentences use 'suggested/proposed', not 'ordered'.

milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Tricky reporting verbs bhi crack kar liye! Ab 'Say vs Tell' ka final confusion clear karte hain!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, ek confusion clear karte hain - 'say' aur 'tell' mein fark kya hai?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir dono ka matlab to 'bolna' hi hota hai na?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Matlab same hai but grammar use alag! 'Say' ke baad DIRECTLY person nahi aata (agar aana ho to 'to' lagta hai) - 'He said to me'. Lekin 'tell' ke baad SEEDHA person aata hai bina 'to' ke - 'He told me'.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir toh 'He told to me' galat hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi, 'told to me' hamesha GALAT hai - ye SBI PO ka classic error-spotting trap hai! Ab poora summary table yaad karo: Statement→said/told(that). Question→asked(if/whether/wh-word). Command→ordered/told(to). Request→requested(to). Suggestion→suggested(that+should). Exclamation→exclaimed(with joy/sorrow). Wish→wished/prayed(that+might).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir itna sara table! Kaise yaad rahega exam mein?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Practice se automatic ho jaata hai - bas sentence ka TYPE pehchano, phir reporting verb khud-ba-khud dimaag mein aa jaayega!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ek quick trick dijiye pehchanne ki!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Chalo test karte hain - agar sentence mein '?' hai to turant dimaag mein 'asked' aana chahiye. Agar '!' ke saath Hurrah/Alas hai to 'exclaimed'. Agar order/command tone hai to 'ordered/told...to'. Yehi hai officer-level speed trick!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ab mujhe lag raha hai main paper mein fatafat pehchan lunga type!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul! Punctuation mark aur pehla word dekhte hi type pehchano, phir formula lagao - yehi hai 3-second officer trick!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir ab error detection wala part shuru karte hain, uski taiyari karni hai!

quiz_payload.question: Choose the correct sentence: 'He ___ me that he was busy.'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'tell' takes the object directly without 'to': 'told me'.

quiz_payload.question: Choose the correct sentence: 'She ___ to her friend that she would come.'
quiz_payload.explanation: 'say' requires 'to' before the person object: 'said to her friend'.

quiz_payload.question: SBI PO style - Spot the error: 'He said to me that he will come tomorrow.' (A) He said to me / (B) that he will come / (C) tomorrow / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: Since 'said' is past tense, 'will' must backshift to 'would'. Correct: 'that he would come'.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab Raju, SBI PO aur Bank exams mein Direct-Indirect speech pe alag hi tarah ka sawal aata hai - 'Error Detection'. Poora sentence diya jaata hai, tumhe GALTI wala part dhundhna hota hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: TRAP 1 - Tense Backshift bhool jaana: Log 'said that he is...' likh dete hain jab 'was' hona chahiye. TRAP 2 - Pronoun mismatch: 'He said that I was happy' jaisa galat sentence - yahan 'I' ki jagah 'he' hona chahiye.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: TRAP 3 - Question mein 'that' ka galat use: 'He asked that where I lived' - GALAT! Question mein 'that' kabhi nahi aata. TRAP 4 - Yes/No question mein 'that' likh dena instead of 'if/whether'.

messages.speaker: raju

TRAP 6 - Question mark ya quotation reh jaana indirect sentence mein - jaise 'He asked if I was fine?' - '?' galat hai, indirect question mein full stop hona chahiye.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection (Q1/6): 'The teacher said that the Earth revolve around the Sun.' Find the error segment.
quiz_payload.explanation: Subject-verb agreement error - it should be 'the Earth revolves' (universal truth, present tense, singular subject).

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection (Q2/6): 'He asked me that why I was crying.' Find the error segment.
quiz_payload.explanation: 'that' should never be used with a Wh-word. Correct: 'He asked me why I was crying.'

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection (Q3/6): 'She told to me that she was leaving.' Find the error segment.
quiz_payload.explanation: 'tell' never takes 'to' before its object. Correct: 'She told me that she was leaving.'

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection (Q4/6): 'He requested me to please help him.' Find the error segment.
quiz_payload.explanation: 'please' must be dropped since 'requested' already conveys politeness. Correct: 'He requested me to help him.'

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection (Q5/6): 'She said that she will meet him the next day.' Find the error segment.
quiz_payload.explanation: 'will' must backshift to 'would' since the reporting verb 'said' is in the past tense.

quiz_payload.question: Error Detection (Q6/6) - BPSC Style Multi-Statement: Read: 'He exclaimed that it was very beautiful scenery and asked that where were we going.' Statement 1: Use of 'very' before 'beautiful' is correct for exclamatory-to-assertive conversion. Statement 2: 'asked that where' is grammatically correct. Which is/are correct?
quiz_payload.explanation: Statement 2 is wrong on two counts - 'that' should not accompany a Wh-word, and the word order should be statement-order 'where we were going', not the inverted 'where were we going'.

revision_points.point: 1st person pronoun changes as per SUBJECT of reporting verb; 2nd person changes as per OBJECT of reporting verb; 3rd person NEVER changes.
Present→Past, Past→Past Perfect; Past Perfect has NO further backshift; Universal truths/habitual facts take NO tense change.
now→then, today→that day, tomorrow→the next day, here→there, this→that, come→go.
can→could, may→might, will→would, shall→should, must→had to (if obligation over); could/would/should/might/ought to remain UNCHANGED.

Statement→said/told(that); Question→asked(if/whether/wh-word, no 'that', no '?'); Command→ordered/told(to); Request→requested(to, drop 'please'); Suggestion/Let's→suggested(that+should); Exclamation→exclaimed(with joy/sorrow, 'very' replaces What/How); Wish→wished/prayed(that+might).

quiz_payload.question:
Assertion (A): The sentence 'He said, "The train leaves at 9 pm daily."' becomes 'He said that the train leaves at 9 pm daily' in indirect speech, without any tense change.
Reason (R): Habitual/scheduled actions and universal truths do not undergo tense backshift in indirect speech.
Choose the correct option:

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

quiz_payload.explanation: A daily scheduled train timing is treated like a habitual fact, so no tense backshift occurs - R correctly explains A.

quiz_payload.question:
Consider the following statements regarding conversion of Interrogative sentences into Indirect Speech:
1. Yes/No questions use 'if' or 'whether' as connectors.
2. Wh-questions retain the question word but drop the auxiliary-subject inversion.
3. The question mark is retained in indirect speech.
4. The reporting verb 'said' changes to 'asked'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
quiz_payload.explanation: Statement 3 is wrong - the question mark is removed and replaced with a full stop in indirect speech.

quiz_payload.question: SBI PO Level - Spot the error: 'The manager insisted that all employees must submitted their reports by evening.' (A) The manager insisted / (B) that all employees must submitted / (C) their reports by evening / (D) No error
quiz_payload.explanation: After the modal 'must', the base form of the verb is used, not the past participle. Correct: 'must submit'.
